claude.sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (25 questions x 6 prompt conditions x 3 reviewers' consensus)

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT patient education responses versus recommended thresholds
links.effect: Reference prompts median FK grade 14.3; Patient-Friendly median 13.2; 6th-grade prompt mean 8.30 and 8th-grade prompt mean 8.06, exceeding targets; only 4th-grade prompts fell below 8th grade (median 5.8).
links.quote: Across all prompt types, readability (measured by Flesch–Kincaid grade level) often exceeded recommended thresholds for patient-directed materials (≤6th grade).

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses relative to health literacy guidelines
links.effect: Most prompts produced collegiate-level outputs versus NIH eighth-grade recommendation; only 4th-grade prompting met guidelines (median FK 5.8) but reduced accuracy.
links.quote: The rest of the prompts had outputs at the collegiate reading levels, which is significantly higher than NIH recommendations.

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT responses when prompted as a low-literacy (4th grade) user
links.effect: 4th-grade prompts were significantly less accurate than Reference (mean diff -0.32, p=0.011) and No Prompting (-0.29, p=0.018); omitted safety information; overall ANOVA F(5,444)=2.45, p=0.033.
links.quote: Tukey's HSD test confirmed that 4th Grade prompts were significantly different from Reference and No Prompting conditions, with estimated mean differences of −0.32 (95 % CI: 0.57 to −0.06, p = 0.011) and −0.29 (95 % CI: 0.54 to −0.04, p = 0.018), respectively.

links.outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT accuracy across equivalent questions with different literacy-level prompt framing
links.effect: Prompt type significantly affected accuracy (F(5,444)=2.45, p=0.033); 4th-grade prompts most variable, scores from 1 to 3, while Reference/No Prompting clustered at ceiling.
links.quote: A one-way ANOVA revealed that prompt type played a role in how accurate responses could be (F(5, 444) = 2.45, p = 0.033).

links.outcome: Completeness and correctness of ChatGPT low back pain answers against guideline-based grading
links.effect: Mean accuracy 2.81/3; under 6% fully incorrect; 18–30% partially correct, mostly omission of key safety considerations.
links.quote: A substantial portion (18–30 %, depending on prompt) were rated as partially correct (score = 2), typically due to omission of key safety considerations or incomplete diagnostic explanations.

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT answers against clinician-graded reference standard (IPSIS guidelines)
links.effect: Overall mean accuracy 2.81 of 3; less than 6% of responses fully incorrect across prompts.
links.quote: Overall, ChatGPT performed high with an average accuracy score of 2.81/3 with less than 6 % of responses rated as fully incorrect.

openai.sample_unit: AI-generated answers (25 questions × 6 prompt types; reviewed by 3 clinicians)

links.effect: 6th-grade prompts mean FK=8.30 (SD=4.47); 8th-grade prompts mean FK=8.06 (SD=3.95), exceeding targets.
links.quote: Despite explicitly prompting ChatGPT to generate responses at a 6th or 8th grade reading level, the Flesch–Kincaid analysis showed that outputs consistently exceeded the targeted complexity: 6th grade prompt group: mean FK grade level = 8.30 (SD = 4.47); 8th grade prompt group: mean FK grade level = 8.06 (SD = 3.95).

links.effect: 4th-grade prompts varied from score 1 to 3 and were significantly lower than Reference and No Prompting conditions.
links.quote: The 4th Grade prompts produced the most variable responses, with scores ranging from 1 (incorrect) to 3 (fully correct).

links.effect: Prompt type was associated with accuracy: F(5, 444) = 2.45, p = 0.033; overall mean accuracy was 2.81/3.
links.quote: A one-way ANOVA, prompt type was significantly associated with accuracy score (F(5, 444) = 2.45, p = 0.033).

links.effect: 18–30% were partially correct depending on prompt, usually from omitted safety considerations or incomplete diagnostic explanations.
links.quote: A substantial portion (18–30 %, depending on prompt) were rated as partially correct (score = 2), typically due to omission of key safety considerations or incomplete diagnostic explanations.

links.effect: Across all prompt types, readability often exceeded recommended patient thresholds (≤6th grade); Reference prompts had median grade level 14.3 (IQR 12.5–17.1) and Patient-Friendly had median 13.2.
links.quote: Across all prompt types, readability (measured by Flesch–Kincaid grade level) often exceeded recommended thresholds for patient-directed materials (≤6th grade).

links.outcome: response accuracy and completeness for lower-literacy prompts
links.effect: Over-simplification to 4th-grade level degraded accuracy; 4th Grade prompts differed significantly from Reference (mean diff −0.32, 95% CI 0.57 to −0.06, p=0.011) and No Prompting (mean diff −0.29, 95% CI 0.54 to −0.04, p=0.018).
links.quote: These findings suggest that over-simplification of ChatGPT's responses (e.g., to a 4th-grade level) degrades ChatGPT's ability to return clinically complete responses.

links.outcome: consistency of accuracy across prompt types
links.effect: Prompt type was significantly associated with accuracy score (F(5, 444) = 2.45, p = 0.033), with 4th Grade prompts producing the most variable responses ranging from 1 to 3.
links.quote: A one-way ANOVA, prompt type was significantly associated with accuracy score (F(5, 444) = 2.45, p = 0.033).
